case_title: DNS Server IP Misconfigured on Clients
ai_proposed_fault: Router-1 has domain lookup disabled globally in IOS configuration.
human_corrected_fault: Client PC-1 is statically configured with non-existent DNS IP 192.168.1.100 instead of active DNS server 192.168.1.10.
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI hallucinated a router-level issue because DNS resolution failed. It ignored explicit client ipconfig evidence showing wrong DNS IP. Executing unnecessary router changes increases operational blast radius.

case_title: Inbound ACL Blocking Web Traffic to Server
ai_proposed_fault: Extended ACL 101 blocks TCP port 80 traffic to 192.168.1.100.
ai_proposed_fix: Router-1(config)# no access-list 101\nRouter-1(config)# access-list 101 permit ip any any
human_corrected_fault: Extended ACL 101 sequence 20 explicitly denies TCP port 80 to web server.
human_corrected_fix:
Router-1(config)# ip access-list extended 101
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# no 20
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# 20 permit tcp any host 192.168.1.100 eq 80
Router-1(config-ext-nacl)# end
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI correctly identified the blocking ACL but suggested wiping the entire ACL 101 and permitting all traffic. This would destroy the perimeter firewall and expose internal DMZ to unauthenticated public attacks.

ai_proposed_fault: DHCP server service hung or lease database corrupted.
human_corrected_fault: DHCP pool is missing 'ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1' causing default gateway IP to be leased to client PC.
human_corrected_fix: Router-1(config)# ip dhcp excluded-address 192.168.1.1 192.168.1.10\nRouter-1(config)# clear ip dhcp binding 192.168.1.1
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI suggested reloading the core router when lease conflict occurred. A reboot causes enterprise downtime and would re-lease the gateway IP immediately upon reboot. Root cause was missing excluded address.

ai_proposed_fault: NAT overload pool exhausted or translation rate-limit hit.
ai_proposed_fix: Router-1(config)# ip nat pool OVERLOAD_POOL 203.0.113.2 203.0.113.2 prefix-length 30
human_corrected_fault: LAN interface Gi0/0 is configured with 'ip nat outside' and WAN Gi0/1 with 'ip nat inside' (inverted roles).
human_corrected_fix:
Router-1(config)# interface Gi0/0
Router-1(config-if)# no ip nat outside
Router-1(config-if)# ip nat inside
Router-1(config-if)# interface Gi0/1
Router-1(config-if)# no ip nat inside
Router-1(config-if)# ip nat outside
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI attempted to replace NAT pool parameters rather than noticing the inverted direction tags on physical interfaces. Modifying the pool would have left the entire site offline.

ai_proposed_fault: Physical Cat5e patch cable has high attenuation or bad crimp; replace cable.
ai_proposed_fix: Replace physical Ethernet patch cable on Switch-1 Fa0/24.
human_corrected_fault: Switch-1 Fa0/24 is hardcoded to Half-Duplex while connected Server NIC is Full-Duplex, causing late collisions.
human_corrected_fix:
Switch-1(config)# interface FastEthernet0/24
Switch-1(config-if)# duplex full
Switch-1(config-if)# speed 100
Switch-1(config-if)# end
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI assumed physical cable damage based on CRC and collision counters without checking the switchport duplex configuration. Changing cable would not fix the hardcoded half-duplex mismatch.

ai_proposed_fault: Trunk encapsulation protocol mismatch between Switch-1 and Switch-2.
human_corrected_fault: VLAN 30 does not exist in Switch-2 VLAN database, making access port Fa0/5 inactive.
safety_rationale_and_learnings: AI hallucinated a legacy Catalyst trunk encapsulation command on modern fixed-configuration switches (where 802.1Q is the only supported standard) and missed that VLAN 30 was completely absent in 'show vlan brief'.
